title: Good morning, {name} (or Good afternoon / Good evening; Dashboard when the person has no name)
summary: The home screen for whoever runs the café or checks its books: today's figures from the books against a usual day and the day's sales target, what needs someone (the alerts), what the figures say in words, the last 14 days, today hour by hour, what sells, the stock, the latest sales and yesterday's brief. Every figure opens what is behind it. Nothing on it changes stock, money or the books; only answering or snoozing an alert writes anything (to the alert and the audit trail).

get_there: Menu → Dashboard (first in the menu). The owner, general manager and branch manager land here after signing in (unless they chose another first screen on My account). Accountants and auditors land on Reports and open the Dashboard from the menu.

Figures need sales; the comparisons with a usual day need at least one of the four same weekdays before today with sales.
The sales target card shows only once a day's sales target is set on Settings → Rules.

parts.name: How the screen is arranged (by role)
parts.shows: Nobody arranges their own dashboard; the app arranges it for the person's most senior role. Owner and general manager: Today, then Needs you, then the rest; the charts in the order the last 14 days, today hour by hour, yesterday's brief; the side column What sells, Stock, Recent sales; the four figures Net sales today, Orders, Average order value, Gross profit. Branch manager: Needs you first, then Today; today hour by hour before the 14 days; Stock, Recent sales, then What sells. Accountant and auditor: Today first; Gross profit leads the figures (then net sales, average order, orders); yesterday's brief leads the charts; Recent sales leads the side. Whoever it is, when any red alert waits, Needs you moves to the very top.

parts.shows: A greeting by the time of day in the café's time zone (morning before 12:00, afternoon before 17:00, evening after), the weekday, date and time, and the place for someone who works at one place.

parts.name: Getting set up
parts.shows: Only while the café is new (no sale yet, or its first sale within the last 30 days), until every step is done or put aside, and only to someone who may do at least one step left. Steps in order: Stock items, Suppliers, Recipes, Menu and prices, Tables, Staff and their PINs, The first sale. Each is ticked once the café has one (with '{n} added', or 'Done' for the first sale); the next step is marked 'Next'. A progress line says '{done} of {total} done'. The owner and the general manager see the full list; anyone else sees it folded to one line: 'Getting set up: {done} of {n} done'.

parts.name: Today: Today's target
parts.shows: Only when a day's net sales target is set (Settings → Rules; for someone who works at one place, the place's own target). It shows today's net sales as the books have them 'of {target}', the share in whole percent rounded down (100% means reached), a bar, and a mark on the bar where a usual day of this weekday would be by now. Worked out: share = today's net sales ÷ target. A usual day = the 4 same weekdays before today, leaving out any with no sales. Usual share by now = what a usual day had sold by this minute ÷ its whole day. Expected by now = target × usual share by now: at or over it, the card says 'Ahead of the pace'; under it, 'Behind the pace' (card marked behind). The day's end if the rest goes as usual = today so far + (usual whole day − usual so far), said to the nearest 1,000. A day with more refunds than sales draws an empty bar.

parts.name: Today: the four figures
parts.shows: Net sales today: revenue in the books today (sales less discounts and refunds; a refund counts on the day it is made). Orders: today's sales not voided and not open. Average order value: net sales ÷ orders, rounded. Gross profit after waste & fees: net sales less everything in cost of sales (cost of goods, price differences on deliveries, platform fees and commission, waste, count differences); shown red below zero, with '{pct}% of net sales'. Under net sales, orders and the average: how today compares with a usual day of this weekday by this time ('{pct}% above usual by {time}', '{pct}% below usual by {time}', or 'As usual by {time}' within 5% either way), and a small line of the 14 days before today. For someone who works at one place, all are that place's.

parts.name: Needs you (the alerts)
parts.shows: Every alert rule is checked against the books each time the dashboard opens: new conditions open an alert, cleared ones disappear by themselves. 🔴 red cannot wait; 🟠 orange can wait. Red alerts are always shown: the first two of each rule on the page, the rest under one red row '{rule}: {n} more'. Orange alerts fold into one row '{n} orange alert(s) can wait for a quiet moment.' with up to four kinds and how many of each; inside, two or more of one rule fold again into a row '{rule}: {n}' with the first one's reason. Each alert shows its title, why it matters, what to do (a link to where to do it, with an arrow), its rule's name, how sure it is (Sure, Fairly sure, Early sign) and 'since {when}' (when first seen). 🔵 'Answered or snoozed ({n})' lists those answered with a note or snoozed: they stay until the condition clears. When nothing waits: '🟢 Nothing needs you'. Every rule is listed under messages below.

controls.label: {action} →
controls.does: Opens the screen where the alert is dealt with (e.g. Journals for the account, Cash sessions, What to buy, Products, Vendors, Approvals, Cash ahead, the watch list).

controls.label: {rule}: {n} more
controls.does: Opens the rest of the red alerts of one rule.

controls.label: {n} orange alert(s) can wait for a quiet moment.
controls.does: Opens the orange alerts.

controls.label: {rule}: {n}
controls.does: Opens the orange alerts of one rule.

controls.label: Answered or snoozed ({n})
controls.does: Opens the alerts already answered or snoozed.

controls.label: Answer
controls.does: Opens a box 'What was done, or why it is fine' with Save the answer and Cancel. On an answered alert the button reads 'Answer again'.
controls.who: Owner, general manager, branch manager, accountant (sale.void or accounting.post). Not shown on an alert about your own exceptions.
controls.rules: The note needs at least 3 characters (the button stays grey until then); at most 300.

controls.label: Save the answer
controls.does: Marks the alert answered with who, when and the note ('Answered by {name} ({when}): “{note}”'); it moves to Answered or snoozed. Shows 'Saving…' while sending.
controls.after: Nothing in stock, money or the books changes. The answer is on the audit trail (alert.acknowledge). The alert stays until its condition clears; if an orange alert turns red, the answer is cleared and it asks again. Yesterday's brief no longer lists an answered red alert under To do.

controls.label: Snooze
controls.does: Opens 'until' with a date (Snooze until) and a box 'Why it can wait', with Snooze it and Cancel.
controls.who: As Answer. Not shown while the alert is snoozed.
controls.rules: The date is from tomorrow to 30 days ahead; a week ahead is offered. The reason needs 3 to 300 characters.

controls.label: Snooze until
controls.does: The day the alert comes back if it is still true.
controls.rules: Tomorrow to 30 days from today; required.

controls.label: Snooze it
controls.does: Puts the alert under Answered or snoozed with 'Snoozed until {day} by {name}: “{reason}”'.
controls.after: Nothing in the books changes. On the audit trail (alert.snooze). It comes back on that day if the condition is still there, at once if an orange alert turns red, and it leaves the brief while snoozed.

controls.label: Cancel
controls.does: Closes the answer or snooze box without saving.

parts.name: Show the rest (phone only)
parts.shows: On a phone the charts and lists below are behind one button; a wider screen shows everything.

controls.label: Show the rest: charts, stock, recent sales
controls.does: Shows the charts and lists; the button then reads 'Show less' and folds them again.

parts.name: What the figures say
parts.shows: The day in words, each with a mark and, where there is one, a link to act on it: how today compares with a usual day of this weekday by now (with '{today} so far; {usual} by then on average, over the {n} before.'), the busiest hour of a usual day, the product that brought in the most over the last 7 days, the product that keeps the least of its price (under 30%, sold at least 3 times, costed), the item that came in dearest over the last 14 days, and the stock below reorder level. Every sentence is listed under messages.

controls.label: (each sentence)
controls.does: Opens where to act: the sales analysis by hour (today), Staff (the busiest hour), the sales analysis by product (7 days), Products (thin margin), the Price watch (dearer deliveries), Inventory (low stock).

parts.name: Sales, the last 14 days
parts.shows: A column for each of the last 14 days' net sales (today marked 'Today'; days below zero drawn empty), each with its weekday, date and '{n} order(s)'. A dashed line 'Average: {amount} a day' is the average of the 13 days before today that had sales.

controls.label: Show as a table
controls.does: Shows the same figures as a table (Day, Net sales).

parts.name: Today, hour by hour
parts.shows: Today's net sales in each hour (hh:00–hh:00 · {n} order(s)), from the first to the last hour any day sold in, with a line 'A usual {weekday}': the average of the same 4 weekdays before, hour by hour. 'No sales yet today.' when there are none.

controls.label: Show as a table
controls.does: Shows the hours as a table (Hour, Today).

parts.name: Yesterday, {weekday} {date} (the daily brief)
parts.shows: Three columns kept apart. Facts: net sales over how many sales, voids, refunds and discounts with their amounts, waste (account 5300), how the drawer was counted (right, short, over, or not counted), and sales with something costed at nothing. Calculations: cost of goods (5000) and its share of net sales; gross profit after waste and every other cost of sales, and its share; last week's same weekday and the change; a usual weekday (average of the four before that had sales). To do: the action of every red alert nobody has answered (at most 5 shown, then '…and {n} more' to Needs you); if none, how many orange alerts wait; else 'Nothing to do.' Under it: 'Open now: 🔴 {red} · 🟠 {orange} — each above, with what to do.'

controls.label: …and {n} more
controls.does: Jumps to Needs you.

parts.name: Watch list card
parts.shows: 'Watch list' and '{n} thing(s) worth a look' when the watch list has open findings. Names are not shown here.

controls.label: Open the watch list
controls.does: Opens Reports → Watch list.
controls.who: Only the owner, and the general manager if the owner allows it.

parts.name: What sells, the last 7 days
parts.shows: The five products that brought in the most net sales from 6 days ago to today, each with '{n} sold · {kept}% kept' (kept = (net − recipe cost) ÷ net) or '{n} sold · not costed yet' when the cost is nothing.

parts.name: Stock value / Stock at {place}
parts.shows: What the stock is worth now (the kept stock balance; for someone at one place, that place's). Below it, items below zero first (red), then those furthest under their reorder level (amber), as 'on hand / reorder level unit', at most 6. 'All above reorder level' when none; 'No items yet.' with no items.

controls.label: Stock value / Stock at {place}
controls.does: Opens Inventory.

controls.label: …and {n} more
controls.does: Opens Inventory for the rest of the low items.

parts.name: Recent sales
parts.shows: The last 6 sales (any day): time, channel, lines as 'name ×qty', a status badge if not completed (e.g. voided, refunded), and the net amount. 'No sales yet.' when there are none.

messages.do: Open the account's journal lines and record where the money really came from. (Link: Journals for that account.)

messages.text: The drawer at {place} has not been counted for {day}
messages.when: Alert 'Drawer not counted' (orange, Sure): one day before today whose cash no closed session or count took in. With two or more days it is red: 'The drawer at {place} has not been counted for {n} days, since {day}'. Why: Until the drawer is counted, nobody knows whether the cash is all there.
messages.do: Close its session on the till, counting the cash; a manager can close one left open on Cash sessions.

messages.text: Session {no} at {place} has been open since {when}
messages.when: Alert 'Cash session left open': a session open longer than 14 hours (setting); red at twice that. Why: The cash in an open session has not been counted: the longer it stays open, the more passes through it unchecked.
messages.do: Close it on the till, counting the cash; a manager can close it on Cash sessions.

messages.text: Session {no} at {place} closed {amount} IQD short
messages.when: Alert 'Cash session short' (Sure), last 7 days: a session closed short by 5,000 IQD or more (setting); red at five times that. Also 'Session {no} at {place} opened {amount} IQD short of what the last session left'. Why: Cash that should be in the drawer is not: change miscounted, a sale not rung up, or money taken.
messages.do: Look at the session's statement on Cash sessions, and ask whoever had the drawer.

messages.text: Session {no} at {place} was closed by {name}: {reason}
messages.when: Alert 'Cash session closed by a manager' (orange), last 7 days. Why: 'It was closed without a count: what it held is counted when the drawer next opens.' or 'Its cashier did not close it: the count was not theirs.'
messages.do: Check it with the cashier on Cash sessions.

messages.text: A stock count has been open since {when}
messages.when: Alert 'Stock count left open' (orange): a count in draft, counting or submitted for more than 8 hours (setting). Why: An open count is not in the books yet, and the longer it stays open the harder it is to finish honestly.
messages.do: Finish it, or cancel it, on Stock Count.

messages.text: {item} runs out in {no time / under a day / n days}: {qty} {unit} left, using about {daily} a day
messages.when: Alert 'Running out': days of cover (on hand ÷ average daily use over the last 14 days) is under the delivery time + 1 day (the last supplier's own, else 1 day). Red under a day. Quiet with under 7 days of history and on a day the item was received. Sure with 28+ days of history, Fairly sure 14–27, Early sign 7–13. Why: What is sold without stock is costed wrongly, and customers are turned away.
messages.do: 'Order about {qty} {unit} (a week of use).' (opens What to buy) or, for an item made here, 'Make a batch on Production.' (opens its stock card).

messages.text: {item}: {qty} {unit} on hand, below its reorder level of {level}
messages.when: Alert 'Below its reorder level' (orange, Sure), unless Running out already names it. Why: Below the reorder level there may not be enough until the next delivery.
messages.do: 'Order it.' (What to buy) or 'Make a batch on Production.'

messages.text: {reason} — confirmed by {name}
messages.when: Alert 'Delivery price confirmed' (orange): in the last 7 days someone confirmed a delivery price far (over 25%) from the item's cost. Shows 'A delivery price was confirmed' when no reason was kept. Why: A price typed wrongly changes the cost of everything made from the item until it is corrected.
messages.do: Check it against the supplier's invoice. (Purchasing)

messages.text: {product} is sold with no recipe: its sales are costed at nothing
messages.when: Alert 'Sold with no recipe' (orange): an active product with no recipe and no reason for using no stock; or '{product} cannot be sold: its recipe has no version in force today'. Why: A sale costed at nothing overstates the profit, and its stock is never taken off the shelf.
messages.do: Give it its recipe on Products, or say why it uses no stock.

messages.text: {product} ({channel}): sold below cost at {price} IQD, costing {cost}
messages.when: Alert 'Margin' (red): the channel price is under today's recipe cost. Why: Every one sold loses money. Fairly sure when an ingredient has none on hand (its cost is the last delivery's).
messages.do: Review the price, or the recipe, on Products.

messages.text: {product} ({channel}): {pct}% margin at {price} IQD, costing {cost}
messages.when: Alert 'Margin' (orange): (price − cost) ÷ price is under the margin target (70%, setting); the % is cut, not rounded. Why: Under the {target}% target, the price no longer covers what the recipe costs now.
messages.do: Review the price, or the recipe, on Products.

messages.text: {item} has no cost yet, and {n} product(s) use(s) it: {names}
messages.when: Alert 'No cost yet' (orange, Sure): an ingredient costed at nothing, named once with up to 4 products (then 'and {n} more'). Why: Every sale that uses it is costed at nothing for it, so its profit is overstated.
messages.do: 'Receive it with its cost, or give it its opening stock, on Inventory.' or, for an item made here, 'Make a batch on Production: its cost comes from its ingredients.'

messages.text: Waste of {amount} IQD in the last 7 days, against about {usual} in a usual week
messages.when: Alert 'Waste above its usual' (orange): waste and losses (5300, 5310) in the last 7 days above 1.5 times a usual week (days 8–35 back) and above 20,000 IQD (settings); needs 14 days of books. Fairly sure with 4 weeks to compare, else Early sign. Why: Waste well above its usual is money leaving through the bin: a delivery gone off, a recipe, or a habit.
messages.do: Look at the waste on Inventory: which items, and who recorded them.

messages.text: {name}: {n} void(s), refund(s), discount(s) or cancelled bill(s) in 7 days, {amount} IQD ({pct}% of their sales)
messages.when: Alert 'Exceptions by one person' (orange, Fairly sure): in 7 days at least 10 (setting), or their amount over 3% of the person's own sales (setting). Why: Most exceptions have good reasons; a pattern is worth a look. This is evidence, not an accusation.
messages.do: Review them on Reports → Exceptions. The person themselves cannot answer it.

messages.text: {amount} IQD of card money is more than {n} days old and not yet recorded as settled
messages.when: Alert 'Card money not banked' (orange, Sure): card takings (1010) older than 3 days (setting) not settled. Why: Card takings should reach the bank within a few days; money that does not may never have been taken.
messages.do: Record the card settlement on Sales, from the terminal's report and the bank statement.

messages.text: {n} {platform} order(s), {amount} IQD, is/are more than {days} days old and not yet paid out; the oldest from {day}
messages.when: Alert 'Platform money not received' (orange, Sure): platform orders not paid out after 7 days (setting). Why: Platform payouts come on a cycle; an order past it may be missing from a statement.
messages.do: Match the platform's statement on Delivery Platforms, and raise any order it left out.

messages.text: {amount} IQD in platform receivable is matched to no order
messages.when: Alert 'Platform money not received' (orange, Fairly sure): 1100 holds more than the orders waiting explain; or 'Platform receivable is {amount} IQD short of the orders waiting to be paid out'. Why: Sales from before order numbers, or a payout recorded by hand, leave platform receivable unexplained by any order.
messages.do: Find the statement it belongs to; correct it with a journal on Journals if it was recorded by hand.

messages.text: {supplier}: {amount} IQD overdue by {n} day(s)
messages.when: Alert 'Supplier bill due' (orange, Sure): a bill not paid in full, due within 3 days (setting) or overdue; also '… due today' and '… due on {day}'. Why: Bills paid late cost goodwill, and sometimes a late fee.
messages.do: Pay it, or agree a date with the supplier, on Vendors.

messages.text: {product} is {high} IQD on {channel} but {low} on {channel}
messages.when: Alert 'Possible price typo' (orange, Fairly sure): one channel's price more than 3 times another's (setting). Why: A price more than three times another channel's is usually a missing or extra zero.
messages.do: Confirm it on Products.

messages.text: Possible duplicate: {account} {amount} IQD in journal {no} ({day}) and journal {no} ({day})
messages.when: Alert 'Possible duplicate payment' (orange, Fairly sure): two expenses, bills or journals to the same running-cost account, same amount, within 3 days, in the last 30, neither reversed (prepaid shares are left out). Why: The same amount to the same account twice in a few days is sometimes paid twice.
messages.do: Confirm both are right, or reverse one on Journals.

messages.text: {item}: {qty} {unit} more used than the recipes say between the counts of {day} and {day} ({pct}%, {amount} IQD)
messages.when: Alert 'Usage unlike the recipes' (Fairly sure): the last two approved counts of an item at a place, the later in the last 14 days, differ from the recipes by at least 10% and 5,000 IQD (settings); red at five times the amount. Also '… less used …'. Why: What the counts say went, less the losses recorded, is more (or less) than the recipes of what was sold and made.
messages.do: Open Usage on Inventory: it shows what came in, what was sold, made and lost between the counts, and what may explain it.

messages.text: {item} is below zero in the books: {qty} {unit}
messages.when: Alert 'Stock below zero' (red, Sure), unless the item's rule allows it. Why: Stock cannot be less than nothing: a delivery or a batch was not entered, or more was used than was recorded.
messages.do: Enter the delivery or the batch that is missing, or count the item on Stock Count.

messages.text: {n} loss(es) waiting for a manager's approval ({amount} IQD)
messages.when: Alert 'Losses waiting for approval' (Sure): losses over the limit saved to wait; red once one has waited 2 days. Why: A loss over the limit was saved to wait for a manager: until one approves it, or reverses it, nobody has looked at it.
messages.do: Open Inventory: approve each loss, or reverse one that did not happen.

messages.text: {item}, batch {no}, is past its use-by: {qty} {unit} left
messages.when: Alert 'Use-by date' (red, Sure). Why: Past its use-by it is not to be sold: what is left is a loss.
messages.do: Record what is left as expired on Inventory, or change its use-by if it was set wrong.

messages.text: {item}, batch {no}, is to be used by {when}: {qty} {unit} left
messages.when: Alert 'Use-by date' (orange): due within 24 hours. Why: What is not used by then is lost.
messages.do: Put it out before newer batches: sales take it first.

messages.text: {name} has been clocked in for {n} hours, since {when}
messages.when: Alert 'Clocked in a long time' (Sure): clocked in longer than the staff rule's hours (16); red after 24 hours. Why: Hours left open are paid as worked: a clock-out forgotten becomes overtime.
messages.do: Clock them out on the till, or correct the hours on Staff.

messages.text: The payroll for {month} is not approved: salaries were due on {day}
messages.when: Alert 'Salaries due' (Sure): from payday (the 1st by default), last month's payroll not drafted or approved; red a week after payday. Why: Until the payroll is approved, the month's salaries are not in the books and nobody can be paid.
messages.do: Draft it on Payroll, check it, and approve it.

messages.text: Salaries for {month}: {amount} IQD not paid yet
messages.when: Alert 'Salaries due': approved but not all paid. Why: Salaries owed and not paid are owed to people who have done the work.
messages.do: Pay them on Payroll.

messages.text: {n} bank line(s), the oldest from {day}, are on no bank statement
messages.when: Alert 'Bank not reconciled' (orange, Sure): bank lines more than 35 days old not on any statement. Why: The bank's own statement shows whether the books have every payment in and out of the bank.
messages.do: Reconcile the bank with its statement on Chart of Accounts.

messages.text: {n} month(s) of prepaid expenses are due to be released, {amount} IQD in all
messages.when: Alert 'Prepaid expenses due' (orange, Sure). Why: Each month a prepaid expense covers takes its share of it: until it is released, that month's profit is too high.
messages.do: Release what is due on Expenses.

messages.text: {n} waiting for a manager's approval: {counts} count(s), {orders} order(s)
messages.when: Alert 'Waiting for approval' (Sure): stock counts submitted or purchase orders waiting; red after a day. Why: A stock count posts nothing, and an order goes to no supplier, until a manager approves it.
messages.do: Open Approvals: approve each one, or send it back with why.

messages.text: The bank would be {amount} short on {day}
messages.when: Alert 'Money short ahead' (Fairly sure): the cash forecast for the next 14 days puts the bank (or 'The safe would be {amount} short on {day}') below nothing; red when it starts within 3 days; only once the books go back 4 weeks. Why: From what it holds now, the usual takings and what is due, as the café's own records have them.
messages.do: As it says: 'Move {amount} from the safe to the bank by {day}.', 'Ask {supplier} to take {amount} later.' or 'Put money in, or pay something due later.' Open Cash ahead.

messages.text: {n} thing(s) on the watch list worth a look
messages.when: Alert 'Worth a look' (orange, Fairly sure): strong findings open on the watch list; no names here. Why: A pattern far from what the others do at the same hours, by more than luck would give.
messages.do: Open the watch list (the owner).

title: Waste by recipe
summary: Four weeks of batches made on Production, recipe by recipe, each followed to now: what was sold or used, thrown away, eaten or given away, and still in stock; what was thrown away cost; and, where it was mostly left unsold, a batch size that would have covered what went. Above it, what was thrown away unsold in the last seven days, item by item, with what to try.

parts.name: Tiles
parts.shows: Thrown away: cost of what the four weeks' batches threw away, with '{pct} of what was made and has gone' (cost thrown ÷ cost of what has left the shelf). Batches made, with '{n} recipe(s)'. Eaten or given away: staff meals, gifts and tastings at the batches' cost. The most thrown away: the recipe with the costliest waste, with '{pct} of what it made and has gone'.

parts.name: What the batches say
parts.shows: For up to 3 recipes that threw away 10% or more of what went: the share and cost, and why (smaller batches would help / it went past its use-by unsold / spilt, melted or spoilt in the making). Then whether nothing or no recipe wasted a tenth, how much was eaten or given, and how many batches are still in stock.

parts.name: What was thrown away, by recipe
parts.shows: Bars of the cost thrown away, the 10 costliest recipes, each with '{pct} of what went, {qty}'. Only when something was thrown away.

parts.name: Recipe by recipe
parts.shows: Recipe (and its item), Batches, Made, Sold or used (sold, or went into other batches), Thrown away (amber at 10% or more) with '{pct} of what went', Eaten or given away, Still in stock, What it cost (thrown away, at each batch's own cost), A better batch (or '—'). Worked out: thrown away = what the batch's lot lost, less what was eaten or given; share = thrown ÷ (made − still in stock). A better batch is shown only when the share is 10% or more, most of the waste went unsold (past use-by, spoilt), at least 2 batches are all gone, and those batches on average sold, used or gave less than they made: the better batch is that average, rounded down.

parts.shows: Columns 'End of {day before From}' and 'End of {To}'. What the café owns: cash accounts (1000 till, 1001, 1005 safe, 1006, 1020 bank) then 'Cash in hand and at the bank'; other current assets then 'Current assets'; 15xx then 'Fixed assets'; 'Total assets'. What the café owes: each liability, 'Total owed'. The owner's: each equity account, 'Profit of earlier years, not yet closed' (only when not nothing), 'Profit this year, not yet closed', 'Total equity', 'Owed and the owner's'. Worked out from every published journal before the day ended: an asset = debits − credits; a liability or equity = credits − debits; profit this year = revenue − expenses from 1 January, not yet closed into Retained earnings (on locking December). summary: Patterns that stand out from what the others do at the same hours, by more than luck would give: sales voided far more often, discounts just under the limit again and again, and the drawer short again and again. Each person is set against the others who sold at the same hours (four-hour bands, by place). Someone new is not judged in their first three weeks. parts.name: Open findings
parts.shows: Strong ones first. Each: a title ('{person}: sales voided far more often than the others' at the same hours', '{person}: discounts just under the limit, again and again', '{person}: the drawer short again and again'), the evidence lines, how unusual ('Strong: less than 1 in a million by luck', 'Worth a look: less than 1 in 100,000 by luck', 'Worth a look: less than 1 in 10,000 by luck') and 'first seen {first}, last {last}'. How it is found: what the others' rate at the same hours would give the person is the expected number; a finding needs at least 8 voids (2.5 times expected) or 8 near-limit discounts with one reason (3 times expected), or 3 short drawers (or 2 on the same weekday and shift), and a chance by luck under 1 in 10,000; strong under 1 in a million.
